title: Generic lisseness for native adic kernels and cokernels on a quasi-compact scheme
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic absolute-value topology, and use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any scheme $X$, let $B_X$ be the sheaf of locally finite continuous $\Omega$-valued functions: its sections on $U$ are continuous functions $|U|\to\Omega$ such that every point has an open neighbourhood on which the values span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space. Restrictions are by precomposition. This is the coefficient construction used in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], applied to $X$ itself. Write $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$. Call an object lisse if it is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $B_U^{\oplus r_U}$ with $r_U$ a finite nonnegative integer, allowed to vary with the covering member $U$. Let $Y$ be a nonempty quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $F,G\in\mathcal A_Y$ be lisse, and let $\varphi:F\to G$ be a morphism. For a scheme morphism $g:V\to Y$, write $g^*H=B_V\otimes_{g^{-1}B_Y}g^{-1}H$ for the module inverse image, with coefficient map given by precomposition [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There exists a nonempty open subscheme $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that both $\ker(j^*\varphi)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(j^*\varphi)$ are lisse in $\mathcal A_U$.

source.place: Lines 228-327, theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_nonempty_isAdicLisseSheaf_kernel_cokernel (declaration at line 232). Its proof uses constant-rank matrix normal form (lines 94-134), rank descent (lines 177-210), openness of rank superlevel sets (lines 55-67), and a finite subcover. Bhatt-Scholze Section 6.8 is motivation, not a coefficient-sheaf comparison.
